spec.title: Campaign 3 · Stage B · Ф6 — the trial (D-C3-9) — phase report
spec.p: _Written 2026-07-12 ~06:44. Owner-facing narrative; the normative record is MT-C3-01 (Recorded runs). Phase **COMPLETE**._

section.title: TL;DR
section.p: Three paid GLM cold-boss sessions over the frozen `mini_logfmt` menu, with the RLM preamble + `fractality gate` in front of them. Two results, one far bigger than the other:

list.item: **The gated arm delegated 44.4% of eligible work (8/18)** vs the naive C2 baseline of 16.7% (3/18) over the same menu — **~2.7×**.

**fractality ran end to end as a product for the first time.** Real GLM workers spawned under real pods, did work, wrote results, ran acceptance, folded into the journal. Three workers completed with a `worker` result; one passed acceptance 1/1.

section.p: Pre-registration MT-C3-01 was committed first (§10.7); RP-C3-2 pre- authorized the spend. ≤8-session cap honoured (3 fired).

section.title: What was done
section.p: Per MT-C3-01: a single gated arm, N=3. Each run = one `glm-5.2[1m]` cold Claude-Code boss (via z.ai, the same CC+z.ai mechanism now used for delegation), an isolated scratch home + a git-staged copy of the `mini_logfmt` crate, and the menu prefixed with `preamble-g.xml` (the frozen instruction to reach for the need-gate verbs). The runner (`run-arm.sh g`) collected the bus facts + escalations + call-tree; the scorer (`score-g.py`) computed the delegation metric + the P-C3 evidence.

Runs: 1 → boss ran out of turns (50) after routing tasks 1 & 4 to two workers; 2 → boss timed out (25 min) with one worker completing task 2 (acceptance 1/1); 3 → boss fanned out to 8 workers, routing tasks 1–4, two completing task 3.

list.item: **Delegation 44.4% vs 16.7%.** This is the headline. A cold boss, told to gate each task and preferring to delegate, routes ~2.7× more eligible work to workers than the C2 baseline boss did. The need-gate + the preamble turn "hand-do everything" into "route the routable." The distractor-KEEP discipline held perfectly (0/9 wrong delegations of tasks 7/8).

**End-to-end works.** More important than the percentage: the whole loop — `fractality gate` → route verdict → `fractality spawn` → mission-control admission → pod launch → a real GLM worker Claude-Code process → work → `result.md` → acceptance commands → `Collected` on the bus → the journal — ran live. Three workers reached `completed` with a worker-authored result; one ran its acceptance green. The machinery Ф1–Ф5 built is not just unit-tested; it runs.

**P-C3-c CONFIRMED** — zero wall-budget overruns; the differentiator axis held. **P-C3-a SUPPORTED** — window-fitting tasks were routed as one call, never over-decomposed. **P-C3-b / P-C3-d INCONCLUSIVE** — the menu never set an output_schema (nothing to validate) and offered no genuine Silo task (nothing to escalate); the escalation + schema seams are built and tested, the trial just didn't exercise them.

**Single arm, N=3, not a fresh 2-arm A/B.** The predictions are observations of the gated system; MT-C2-01 arm A is the naive comparator over the identical menu. Halved the spend (3 vs 6 sessions) — the RP1/RP5 "sufficient, not super-large" posture.

**A frozen preamble is a controlled variable.** C2's F23 showed a `-p` boss must be TOLD to reach for the verbs. `preamble-g.xml` is committed verbatim so the trial is reproducible and the instruction is not a confound hidden in a transcript.

**The smoke-test-first discipline.** Run 1 was treated as a readiness probe: I confirmed the system ran end to end (gate → spawn → real worker → collect) before committing the rest of the budget. It did; runs 2–3 followed. Had run 1 shown a broken pod launch or env, I would have stopped and reported rather than burn the cap.

**Turn caps dominated completion.** Boss 50 turns, worker 30 turns — bosses timed out mid-menu, workers mid-task. `delegated` (8) is measured honestly; `delegated-AND-collected` (3) is lower purely because of the caps, not the fabric. Raising the worker cap (and/or a larger boss budget) is a one-line config for a future trial; deliberately NOT changed mid-frozen-protocol.

**P-C3-b and P-C3-d were never exercised.** The menu has no structured-output task (schema gate) and no genuine chunk-destroying Silo task (escalation). Both seams are built + unit-tested; a *future* menu with one explicit JSON-schema task and one whole-repo reasoning task would test them. This is a menu-design gap, filed as trial follow-up.

**The gate's decision journal is under-read.** The boss ran `fractality gate --record`, but there is no `fractality decisions` CLI to read the journal back; the scorer leans on the transcript. A tiny `decisions` verb (mirror of `escalations`) would make P-C3-a a hard number next time.

**Absolute delegation is still < 50%.** 44.4% is a big lift over the baseline, but a boss that fully trusted the fabric would be higher; the caps + the C2 "workers can't self-verify" friction (F24) still pull it down.

**The pilot proved itself.** fractality's whole reason to exist — boss delegates to cheap workers under other providers, exchanging through files — happened, live, and moved the delegation number by 2.7×. That is the strongest possible signal that the Stage-B design is sound.

**The delegation-mechanism switch (opencode → CC+z.ai) paid off twice:** it unblocked this session's own grunt delegation AND it is *the same mechanism the trial arms run on*. The pilot eats its own dog food end to end.

**Next trial's menu is the lever.** To test all four predictions and push delegation higher, the menu needs: an explicit structured-output task (P-C3-b), a genuine Silo task (P-C3-d), higher worker turn caps, and a `decisions` read verb. All small, all deferred to a future trial — Stage B's job was to build the machinery and prove it runs, which it did.

section.title: Next
section.p: **Ф7 — close Stage B:** verdicts, the deferrals ledger, the campaign-close report, WAL. Then the follow-on goal: **PP-003 (Option C — the advisor slice, D-C3-7).**
